SQL:
WITH __slayer_stage_cr AS (
  SELECT
    _stage_inner."orders.customers.regions.name" AS "customers__regions__name",
    _stage_inner."orders.customers.city" AS "customers__city",
    _stage_inner."orders.rev" AS "rev"
  FROM (
    SELECT
      customers__regions.name AS "orders.customers.regions.name",
      customers.city AS "orders.customers.city",
      CAST(SUM(orders.amount) AS DOUBLE) AS "orders.rev"
    FROM orders AS orders
    LEFT JOIN customers AS customers
      ON orders.customer_id = customers.id
    LEFT JOIN regions AS customers__regions
      ON customers.region_id = customers__regions.id
    GROUP BY
      customers__regions.name,
      customers.city
  ) AS _stage_inner
)
SELECT
  cr.customers__regions__name AS "cr.customers__regions__name",
  CAST(AVG(cr.rev) AS DOUBLE) AS "cr.avg_city_rev",
  COUNT(*) AS "cr.n"
FROM __slayer_stage_cr AS cr
GROUP BY
  cr.customers__regions__name
LIMIT 21

args.message: I added up order amounts for each city, then took a simple average of those city totals within each region, so every city counts once. North has the highest average city revenue at about 36,444.92 across 3 cities, followed by South (about 34,756.63, 3 cities), East (about 34,369.35, 2 cities) and West (about 24,575.90, 2 cities). Orders whose customer has no known region are grouped together on the null row: about 596.65 on average across 2 city groups. I didn't check what makes up those two groups, so one of them may be orders with a blank city or no matching customer rather than a real city.
